# 14-PREFERENCES-PANEL-IMPLEMENTATION-PLAN.md

**Preferences / Options Panel Implementation Plan**  
**Date:** 2026-04-18  
**Status:** Ready for execution  
**Scope:** Registry Viewer (`apps/registry-viewer/`) + future Legendary Arena game UI  
**Generated by:** Claude (refined by Grok)

---

## 0. Executive Summary

The Registry Viewer currently ships with every user-facing behavior hardcoded: ~40 eagerly-loaded card sets, a fixed dark theme, fixed grid tile size, fixed type-group labels and emojis, hardcoded keyboard shortcuts, and no way for end users to customize anything short of editing `public/registry-config.json` and rebuilding.

This plan introduces a **Preferences / Options Panel**, backed by a **Pinia store** with **localStorage persistence** and optional **URL query-param hydration** for shareable links. The store's type-safe schema is designed to be shared with a future Legendary Arena game UI (`apps/game-ui/`, not created yet) so that both apps can read from the same preferences contract.

The rollout is sequenced across four phases (foundation → panel shell → feature wiring → polish & cross-app sync) and decomposed into **11** discrete work packets (WP-068 … WP-078) suitable for splitting across one or more contributors. Today the only shared workspace package is `packages/registry`; this plan adds a second: `packages/ui-preferences`.

### 0.1 How to Use This Document

- **Solo-dev path:** read §1 to understand what's being changed, skim §2 for the architectural shape, then work through §8 (Work Packets) top-to-bottom. Each WP is self-contained — complete its acceptance criteria before starting the next. §9 (Execution Checklists) is the verification list at the end of each phase; tick every box before moving on.
- **Converting WPs to GitHub issues:** one WP = one issue. Issue title matches the WP heading (e.g. "WP-071 — Wire the **Display** section end-to-end"). Paste the WP's Description, Estimate, Dependencies, and Acceptance Criteria verbatim into the issue body. Apply labels `preferences`, `phase-N`, and the estimate (`3pt`, `5pt`, etc.). Link dependencies via GitHub's "Development" side-panel or a `Depends on #NN` line at the top of the body.
- **Keeping `docs/00-INDEX.md` in sync:** add one line — `- [14-PREFERENCES-PANEL-IMPLEMENTATION-PLAN.md](14-PREFERENCES-PANEL-IMPLEMENTATION-PLAN.md) — Preferences / Options Panel design and execution plan` — to the appropriate section of the index the first time you land a WP from this plan. The final item in the Phase 4 checklist re-verifies this.

## 2. Recommended Architecture

### 2.1 High-level approach

- Introduce **Pinia** as the single state-management primitive (currently absent — the only workspace package today is `packages/registry`).
- Create a `usePreferencesStore` Pinia store with a strictly-typed schema, one action per logical preference, and a top-level `$reset()` plus per-section reset helpers.
- Persist the store to `localStorage` behind a **versioned envelope** (`{ version: 2, prefs: {…} }`) so schema migrations are explicit, not implicit.
- Expose a whitelist of preferences through URL query params for shareable links (e.g. `?view=themes&density=compact&sort=name-asc`). URL takes precedence over localStorage on first load; then user interaction writes back to both.
- Validate hydrated preferences through a **Zod schema** (Zod is already a dependency in both `packages/registry` and `apps/registry-viewer`).
- Use a **section-registry pattern**: shared sections (Appearance, Accessibility) and app-specific sections (Display, Filters, Data Source for the viewer; Gameplay, Sound, etc. for the future game UI) are registered at bootstrap. The panel UI iterates the registry with zero app-specific code paths.

**Two delivery paths — pick one up front:**

> **Option A — Simple (recommended for MVP):** put everything inside `apps/registry-viewer/src/prefs/` first (schema, store, panel, sections, composables). Nothing new in `packages/`. Fastest path to a working panel; minimal monorepo wiring. When the game UI work begins, lift the shared pieces into `packages/ui-preferences/` as a one-shot refactor (the §2.8 tier table tells you exactly which files move).
>
> **Option B — Full shared package (maximum future-proofing):** create `packages/ui-preferences/` from WP-068 and import it from the viewer immediately. Section-registry pattern is first-class from day one; no later hoist; game UI imports the same package when it lands. Slightly more scaffolding in WP-068 but zero drift risk.
>
> **Default:** Option B for teams with a committed game UI roadmap; Option A for solo/iterative work where the game UI is speculative. WP-068 supports both — the "Option A start, Option B hoist later" path is explicitly tested against the same acceptance criteria (only the file locations differ). The rest of this document describes **Option B** paths; to read it as Option A, mentally replace `packages/ui-preferences/src/` with `apps/registry-viewer/src/prefs/shared/`.

### 2.3 Schema contract (TypeScript + Zod)

**Every default below is chosen to match current hardcoded behavior so that a fresh visitor with no stored preferences sees the exact same UI that ships today.** Notable calibrations: `sortField` defaults to `"native"` (the order `reg.listCards()` already returns — no client-side reordering) to preserve audit-item #15 bit-for-bit; `density: "comfortable"` maps to the existing `0.75rem` grid gap; `tileSize: 130` matches the current `minmax(130px, 1fr)`.

```ts
// packages/ui-preferences/src/schema/base.schema.ts  (Option B)
// or apps/registry-viewer/src/prefs/schema/*.ts      (Option A — one file per section)
import { z } from "zod";

export const PREFERENCES_SCHEMA_VERSION = 2;

export const DisplayPrefsSchema = z.object({
  defaultView: z.enum(["cards", "themes"]).default("cards"),
  cardLayout: z.enum(["grid", "list"]).default("grid"),
  tileSize: z.number().int().min(90).max(240).default(130),              // matches minmax(130px, 1fr)
  density: z.enum(["compact", "comfortable", "spacious"]).default("comfortable"),  // 0.75rem gap today
  showTypeBadge: z.boolean().default(true),
  showHeroSubname: z.boolean().default(true),
  showCost: z.boolean().default(true),
  showRarityDot: z.boolean().default(true),
  showHcTag: z.boolean().default(true),
  lazyLoadImages: z.boolean().default(true),                             // matches loading="lazy"
});

export const FiltersPrefsSchema = z.object({
  defaultTypes: z.array(z.string()).default([]),                         // matches empty Set()
  defaultSet: z.string().default(""),                                    // matches filterSet = ""
  defaultHeroClass: z.string().default(""),                              // matches filterHC = ""
  searchMode: z.enum(["substring", "prefix", "fuzzy"]).default("substring"),  // matches nameContains
  searchFields: z.array(z.enum(["name", "text", "hero", "tags"])).default(["name"]),  // matches nameContains
  // "native" = whatever order reg.listCards() returns; preserves audit-item #15
  sortField: z.enum(["native", "name", "set", "cost", "rarity", "heroClass", "type"]).default("native"),
  sortDirection: z.enum(["asc", "desc"]).default("asc"),                 // ignored when sortField === "native"
  persistLastFilters: z.boolean().default(false),                        // today, filters reset on reload
});

export const DataSourcePrefsSchema = z.object({
  metadataBaseUrlOverride: z.string().url().or(z.literal("")).default(""),
  imageBaseUrlOverride: z.string().url().or(z.literal("")).default(""),
  // NEW preference — registry-config.json has no dataVersion today. Empty string means
  // "no cache-busting query appended" which matches current network behavior exactly.
  dataVersionOverride: z.string().default(""),
  enabledSets: z.array(z.string()).default([]),                          // empty = use registry-config.json eagerLoad
  loadThemes: z.boolean().default(true),                                 // matches unconditional getThemes() today
});

export const AppearancePrefsSchema = z.object({
  themeMode: z.enum(["dark", "light", "system"]).default("dark"),        // dark is the only theme today
  accentColor: z.string().regex(/^#[0-9a-f]{6}$/i).default("#7070e0"),   // current .card-tile.selected border
  fontScale: z.number().min(0.75).max(1.5).default(1.0),
  fontFamily: z.enum(["system", "sans", "serif", "mono"]).default("system"),  // inherits browser default today
});

export const AccessibilityPrefsSchema = z.object({
  reduceMotion: z.enum(["auto", "on", "off"]).default("auto"),           // "auto" honors prefers-reduced-motion
  smoothScroll: z.boolean().default(true),                               // matches scrollIntoView behavior: "smooth"
  focusRingBold: z.boolean().default(false),
  glossaryShortcut: z.string().default("Mod+K"),                         // matches Ctrl/Cmd+K today
  escapeClosesLightboxFirst: z.boolean().default(true),                  // matches current Esc order
  showFloatingGlossaryFab: z.enum(["auto", "always", "never"]).default("auto"),  // "auto" = < 1024px, matches today
});

export const AdvancedPrefsSchema = z.object({
  debugPanelOnLoad: z.boolean().default(false),
  verboseDevLog: z.boolean().default(false),
  showRawCardJson: z.boolean().default(false),
  experimentalFeatures: z.record(z.boolean()).default({}),
});

export const PreferencesSchema = z.object({
  version: z.literal(PREFERENCES_SCHEMA_VERSION),
  display: DisplayPrefsSchema,
  filters: FiltersPrefsSchema,
  dataSource: DataSourcePrefsSchema,
  appearance: AppearancePrefsSchema,
  accessibility: AccessibilityPrefsSchema,
  advanced: AdvancedPrefsSchema,
});

export type Preferences = z.infer<typeof PreferencesSchema>;
```

### 2.4 Persistence strategy

| Concern | Decision |
|---|---|
| Storage key | `legendary-arena.preferences` (single-app) or `legendary-arena.prefs.{shared,viewer,game}` (WP-078 split) |
| Envelope | `{ version, prefs }` — version integer, prefs validated by Zod |
| Migration | `migratePreferences(raw: unknown): Preferences` — sequential `v1 → v2 → …` functions |
| Corruption | On Zod failure: log via `devLog`, reset to defaults, keep backup under `legendary-arena.preferences.backup` |
| Quota | Wrap all `localStorage.setItem` calls in try/catch; on `QuotaExceededError` surface a toast and continue in-memory |
| Private mode | Detect `localStorage` unavailability; degrade to in-memory only, disable export/import |

### 2.5 URL sync strategy

- Only a **whitelist** of preferences syncs to URL — `defaultView`, `cardLayout`, `density`, `sortField`, `sortDirection`, `defaultTypes` (comma-joined), `defaultSet`, `defaultHeroClass`, `searchMode`, plus current `search` text.
- Precedence on first mount: **URL > localStorage > defaults**.
- After mount, user mutations write to the store first; a debounced (250 ms) `history.replaceState` writes to URL. Only whitelisted keys are serialized.
- A "Copy shareable link" button in the panel builds a URL from the current non-default preferences only (short URLs).

### 2.6 Reactivity

- `App.vue` reads `usePreferencesStore()` directly (or via `usePreferences()` composable).
- Filters pane removes local refs `searchText / filterSet / filterHC / selectedTypes / activeView` and replaces them with `storeToRefs()` bindings — all filtering becomes reactive to preference changes with no extra wiring.
- `useThemeVars()` installs a `watchEffect` that writes computed values to CSS custom properties on `document.documentElement`:
  - `--bg-base`, `--fg-base`, `--accent`, `--font-scale`, `--tile-min-width`, `--tile-gap`.
- All scoped styles using literal colors migrate to `var(--accent, #7070e0)` fallbacks incrementally (tracked under WP-075).

### 2.7 Future-proofing

- Under Option B, all schema and control primitives ship in `packages/ui-preferences/` from WP-068 — no later hoist, no drift between apps.
- Under Option A, the same files live in `apps/registry-viewer/src/prefs/shared/` until the game UI needs them; the hoist is a pure file-move because no import path crosses `apps/` boundaries.
- The panel UI iterates a **section registry** at runtime: each app calls `registerSection(id, schema, component)` during bootstrap. Adding a new category is "define a Zod schema + register it" with zero changes to the shared `PreferencesPanel.vue`.
- Schema files are **pure** — no Vue or DOM imports — so Node-only consumers (future CLI tools, server-side rendering of shareable links, validation in CI) can read preferences without pulling in a UI framework.

### 2.8 Shared vs app-specific preferences

The preferences surface is split into two tiers. Shared tier lives in `packages/ui-preferences/` (Option B) or `apps/registry-viewer/src/prefs/shared/` (Option A) and is consumed by every app. App-specific tier lives in each app and is registered at bootstrap.

| Tier | Section | Keys | Owner |
|---|---|---|---|
| Shared | Appearance | `themeMode`, `accentColor`, `fontScale`, `fontFamily` | `packages/ui-preferences/` |
| Shared | Accessibility (base) | `reduceMotion`, `smoothScroll`, `focusRingBold`, `escapeClosesLightboxFirst` | `packages/ui-preferences/` |
| Shared | Advanced (base) | `verboseDevLog` | `packages/ui-preferences/` |
| Viewer-specific | Display | `defaultView`, `cardLayout`, `tileSize`, `density`, `showTypeBadge`, `showHeroSubname`, `showCost`, `showRarityDot`, `showHcTag`, `lazyLoadImages` | `apps/registry-viewer/` |
| Viewer-specific | Filters | `defaultTypes`, `defaultSet`, `defaultHeroClass`, `searchMode`, `searchFields`, `sortField`, `sortDirection`, `persistLastFilters` | `apps/registry-viewer/` |
| Viewer-specific | Data Source | `metadataBaseUrlOverride`, `imageBaseUrlOverride`, `dataVersionOverride`, `enabledSets`, `loadThemes` | `apps/registry-viewer/` |
| Viewer-specific | Advanced (app) | `debugPanelOnLoad`, `showRawCardJson`, `glossaryShortcut`, `showFloatingGlossaryFab` | `apps/registry-viewer/` |
| Game-specific (future) | Gameplay | animation speed, hand layout, confirmation dialogs, auto-pass, log verbosity, in-game keybindings | `apps/game-ui/` |
| Game-specific (future) | Sound | master volume, SFX toggle, music toggle | `apps/game-ui/` |

**Registration pattern:**

```ts
// packages/ui-preferences/src/index.ts (shared)
registerSharedSection("appearance",    AppearancePrefsSchema,    AppearanceSection);
registerSharedSection("accessibility", AccessibilityPrefsSchema, AccessibilitySection);
registerSharedSection("advancedBase",  AdvancedBasePrefsSchema,  AdvancedBaseSection);

// apps/registry-viewer/src/prefs/registerSections.ts
registerSection("display",    DisplayPrefsSchema,    DisplaySection);
registerSection("filters",    FiltersPrefsSchema,    FiltersSection);
registerSection("dataSource", DataSourcePrefsSchema, DataSourceSection);
registerSection("advanced",   AdvancedPrefsSchema,   AdvancedSection);

// apps/game-ui/src/prefs/registerSections.ts  (when the game UI exists)
registerSection("gameplay", GameplayPrefsSchema, GameplaySection);
registerSection("sound",    SoundPrefsSchema,    SoundSection);
```

**Key consequence:** each app ends up with one panel instance showing its own mix of shared + private sections. Users get consistency where it matters (theme, a11y) and app-specific controls where they belong. Neither app can see or mutate the other's private sections at compile time — each app's Preferences type is `SharedPrefs & AppPrefs`, computed from what it registered.

**Storage isolation by default:** each app uses its own localStorage key (`legendary-arena.prefs.viewer`, `legendary-arena.prefs.game`). The shared-tier keys are duplicated (not aliased) across storage — cross-app sync is opt-in and is covered by WP-078.

```diff

+import { createPinia } from "pinia";

 import App from "./App.vue";

-createApp(App).mount("#app");
```

### 3.3 `packages/ui-preferences/src/store/createPreferencesStore.ts` (new file, Option B)

Under Option A, save the same file as `apps/registry-viewer/src/prefs/shared/store/createPreferencesStore.ts`. Lives in the shared package; factory that each app calls with its own registered sections.

```ts
import { defineStore } from "pinia";
import { reactive, readonly, watch } from "vue";
import {
  PreferencesSchema,
  PREFERENCES_SCHEMA_VERSION,
  type Preferences,
} from "../schema/base.schema";
import { devLog } from "./_devLog";  // or injected by the consuming app

const STORAGE_KEY = "legendary-arena.preferences";
const BACKUP_KEY = "legendary-arena.preferences.backup";

/** Build a fully-populated defaults object by parsing an empty object. */
function buildDefaults(): Preferences {
  return PreferencesSchema.parse({
    version: PREFERENCES_SCHEMA_VERSION,
    display: {}, filters: {}, dataSource: {},
    appearance: {}, accessibility: {}, advanced: {},
  });
}

function loadFromStorage(): Preferences {
  try {
    const raw = localStorage.getItem(STORAGE_KEY);
    if (!raw) return buildDefaults();
    const parsed = JSON.parse(raw);
    const migrated = migratePreferences(parsed);
    return PreferencesSchema.parse(migrated);
  } catch (error) {
    // why: corrupt preferences should never brick the UI. Back up the bad
    // blob so support can inspect it, then return defaults.
    devLog("prefs", "failed to load preferences; resetting", error);
    try {
      const raw = localStorage.getItem(STORAGE_KEY);
      if (raw) localStorage.setItem(BACKUP_KEY, raw);
    } catch { /* ignore */ }
    return buildDefaults();
  }
}

function migratePreferences(raw: unknown): Preferences {
  // v1 → v2 would go here. For the first shipping version, just pass through.
  return raw as Preferences;
}

export const usePreferencesStore = defineStore("preferences", () => {
  const state = reactive<Preferences>(loadFromStorage());

  /** Persist any changes with quota guard. */
  watch(
    () => JSON.stringify(state),
    (serialized) => {
      try {
        localStorage.setItem(STORAGE_KEY, serialized);
      } catch (error) {
        devLog("prefs", "failed to persist preferences", error);
      }
    },
    { flush: "post" }
  );

  function resetAll() {
    Object.assign(state, buildDefaults());
  }
  function resetSection<K extends keyof Preferences>(section: K) {
    const defaults = buildDefaults();
    (state as any)[section] = defaults[section];
  }
  function importJson(json: string): boolean {
    try {
      const parsed = PreferencesSchema.parse(JSON.parse(json));
      Object.assign(state, parsed);
      return true;
    } catch (error) {
      devLog("prefs", "import failed", error);
      return false;
    }
  }
  function exportJson(): string {
    return JSON.stringify(state, null, 2);
  }

  return { state: readonly(state), mutable: state, resetAll, resetSection, importJson, exportJson };
});
```

### 3.4 `usePreferences.ts` composable (shared)

A thin wrapper so components never import the store directly (easier to swap later):

```ts
import { storeToRefs } from "pinia";
import { usePreferencesStore } from "../store/createPreferencesStore";

export function usePreferences() {
  const store = usePreferencesStore();
  return { ...storeToRefs(store), store };
}
```

### 3.5 `useThemeVars.ts` composable (shared)

Applies appearance preferences to the DOM via CSS variables — single `watchEffect` writing `--bg-base`, `--fg-base`, `--accent`, `--font-scale`, `--tile-min-width`, `--tile-gap` to `document.documentElement.style`.

### 3.6 `apps/registry-viewer/src/App.vue` changes

- Import `usePreferences()` at the top of `<script setup>`.
- Replace local `searchText`, `filterSet`, `filterHC`, `selectedTypes`, `activeView` refs with store-backed refs (preserving their existing shapes).
- Add a gear-icon button to `.header-actions` that toggles a new `preferencesOpen` ref.
- Mount `<PreferencesPanel v-model:open="preferencesOpen" />` once at the root.
- Gate the keyboard shortcut handler on `store.state.accessibility.glossaryShortcut`.

### 3.7 `apps/registry-viewer/src/components/CardGrid.vue` changes

- Read `tileSize`, `density`, `showTypeBadge`, `showHeroSubname`, `showCost`, `showRarityDot`, `showHcTag`, `lazyLoadImages` from `usePreferences()`.
- Replace `minmax(130px, 1fr)` with `minmax(var(--tile-min-width, 130px), 1fr)` and `gap: var(--tile-gap, 0.75rem)`.
- Wrap conditionally-visible meta elements with `v-if`.

### 3.8 `PreferencesPanel.vue` (new, shared)

Full drawer UI — see §4 for layout detail. Iterates the section registry and renders each registered section into a collapsible group.

### 3.9 `apps/registry-viewer/src/lib/theme.ts` changes

- Surface `LAYOUT_VERSION` and all color constants via an exported `themeTokens` object so the preferences panel can introspect them for the advanced color overrides.
- Leave the existing `loadStoredWidth` path untouched for backwards compatibility; deprecate it in a later phase after the preferences store owns width persistence.

### 3.10 URL-sync hook into `onMounted`

```ts
import { useUrlSync } from "@legendary-arena/ui-preferences";  // Option B
onMounted(() => {
  useUrlSync(); // hydrates from URL first, then writes back on changes
  /* existing registry + theme loaders unchanged */
});
```

## 4. UI/UX Design of the Panel

### 4.1 Entry point

- Gear-icon button (`⚙️`) added to `.header-actions`, left of `📖 Glossary`.
- `aria-label="Open preferences"`; tooltip "Preferences (Ctrl+,)".
- Keyboard shortcut: `Ctrl/Cmd + ,` (standard, matches VS Code / Chrome).

### 4.2 Layout (desktop)

Right-side drawer, 420 px wide, full viewport height, slides in over a 40 %-opacity backdrop that does **not** block the viewer (card grid stays legible).

```
┌───────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ ⚙ Preferences                          ✕ │  ← sticky header with close + reset-all kebab
├───────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ ▸ Display                                 │  ← collapsible sections
│ ▸ Sorting & Filtering Defaults            │
│ ▸ Data Source                          ⚠️ │  ← warning badge for advanced section
│ ▸ Appearance                              │
│ ▸ Accessibility & Behavior                │
│ ▸ Advanced / Debug                     🧪 │
├───────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ [ Reset all ]  [ Export ]  [ Import ]     │  ← sticky footer
│ [ Copy shareable link ]                   │
└───────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

### 4.3 Section interaction

- Section header shows name, a **per-section reset** button (only enabled when section differs from defaults), and a chevron.
- Controls within a section are right-aligned; label text left-aligned for scanability.
- Each control has a subtle help icon (`ⓘ`) opening a short tooltip with the preference's effect.

### 4.4 Control primitives

| Primitive | Used for |
|---|---|
| `PreferenceToggle` | Boolean (`showTypeBadge`, `lazyLoadImages`, `smoothScroll`) |
| `PreferenceSelect` | Enum (`defaultView`, `cardLayout`, `density`, `themeMode`, `sortField`) |
| `PreferenceSlider` | Numeric (`tileSize`, `fontScale`) — displays current value and default |
| `PreferenceColor` | Hex color (`accentColor`) — advanced only |
| `PreferenceChipGroup` | Multi-select (`searchFields`, `defaultTypes`) |
| `PreferenceTextInput` | URL overrides, data-version tag, keyboard shortcut capture |

### 4.5 Mobile plan (< 768 px)

- Drawer becomes **bottom sheet** occupying 90 % of viewport height, dragged to dismiss.
- Sections become flat (no collapse) with larger 48 px-tall rows.
- Sticky footer remains; "Copy shareable link" replaced with a share-sheet button on iOS/Android.
- Entry point: replace `⚙` header button with a second FAB, bottom-left (mirror of `📖` FAB on the right). The FAB auto-hides when the glossary FAB is hidden.

### 4.6 Dirty state

- Red dot on the gear icon when any preference differs from defaults.
- Section chevrons show a small `●` when that section has non-default values.

### 4.7 Accessibility

- Drawer root is `role="dialog"`, `aria-modal="true"`, `aria-labelledby="prefs-title"`.
- Focus trap while open; returns focus to gear button on close.
- First focusable element is the close button.
- Escape closes the drawer (regardless of `escapeClosesLightboxFirst` — preferences outranks glossary).
- Every control has an associated `<label for>` or `aria-labelledby`.

---

## 5. Edge Cases & Best Practices

### 5.1 Data version handling

- `dataVersionOverride` is a **new** runtime-only preference — `registry-config.json` has no `dataVersion` key today, so the feature is entirely additive.
- Empty string ⇒ no cache-busting query appended (matches current network behavior exactly).
- Non-empty ⇒ append `?v={value}` to every metadata and image fetch URL to bypass CDN cache.
- Change takes effect on next full reload only; panel shows an inline "Reload required" banner with a Reload button.
- **Optional future step (not in this plan):** if a `dataVersion` field is later added to `registry-config.json`, prefer the config value when `dataVersionOverride` is empty and the config field is non-empty; override wins only when non-empty.

### 5.2 Set eager-load overrides

- If `enabledSets` is a strict **subset** of the default `eagerLoad`, surface a warning: "X sets disabled — some themes and cards won't appear."
- If `enabledSets` is empty, use the `registry-config.json` default (do not fall through to "no sets").
- Unknown set abbreviations are silently dropped at parse time; log via `devLog`.

### 5.3 Base URL overrides

- Validated against `z.string().url()`; rejected values never enter state.
- Panel explicitly warns: "Only change this if you know what you're doing — broken URLs will blank the viewer."
- Reset-section button is always one click away.

### 5.4 Performance

- `watch(() => JSON.stringify(state))` is O(schema) per mutation. For this schema (~30 scalars) it is dominated by the `localStorage.setItem` call itself and acceptable. If the schema doubles, migrate to a keyed `watch` per section.
- CSS variables are applied via a single `watchEffect` that batches writes inside one `requestAnimationFrame`.
- `useUrlSync` debounces URL writes at 250 ms so rapid slider drags don't flood `history.replaceState`.
- `PreferencesPanel.vue` uses `v-show="open"` after first open (lazy) to avoid paying mount cost before first use.

### 5.5 Testing

- Schema unit tests: assert every default survives a round-trip through `JSON.stringify` + `PreferencesSchema.parse`.
- **Defaults-match-today test:** for each preference, assert the default value produces the same DOM output as the current hardcoded equivalent (snapshot comparison on `CardGrid` and `App`).
- Migration tests: `migratePreferences(v1Blob)` returns a valid `v2` shape.
- Store tests: `resetSection("display")` clears display but leaves filters untouched.
- Component tests (Vitest + Vue Test Utils): toggling `showTypeBadge` removes the `.type-badge` node from `CardGrid`.
- URL-sync tests: given `?view=themes&sort=name-desc`, store hydrates those values and nothing else.
- Accessibility tests: `axe-core` run on the open `PreferencesPanel` for zero violations.
- Manual smoke: Firefox private mode (no localStorage), quota-full Chromium, iOS Safari bottom-sheet dismissal.

### 5.6 Type safety

- No `any` anywhere in the new files; `as any` only permitted in `resetSection` due to TS narrowing limitation across generic indexed writes, and is covered by unit tests.
- Components import `Preferences` / `Preferences["display"]` etc. — never raw strings.
- `devLog` category `"prefs"` reserved for this subsystem.

### 5.7 Backward compatibility

- `LAYOUT_VERSION` localStorage key remains owned by `theme.ts` for now. WP-077 formally migrates panel widths into the preferences store.
- Existing users with no stored preferences see the **exact same UI** they see today (all defaults chosen to match current hardcoded values — see §2.3 annotations).

---

## 6. Implementation Roadmap

### Phase 1 — Foundation (WP-068, WP-069)

Create the shared `packages/ui-preferences/` workspace package up front (Option B) or the equivalent `apps/registry-viewer/src/prefs/shared/` tree (Option A). Install Pinia in the viewer, wire `createPinia()`, add the gear icon with a stub panel that only shows "Reset all" and "Export / Import". No existing behavior changes yet. Ship a feature-flagged build.

### Phase 2 — Panel shell & Display section (WP-070, WP-071)

Build the remaining control primitives. Wire the **Display** section end-to-end in the viewer so users can change tile size, density, badge visibility, and default view. Remove the corresponding hardcoded values from `App.vue` and `CardGrid.vue`.

### Phase 3 — Filters, Data Source, Accessibility (WP-072, WP-073, WP-074, WP-076)

Wire the remaining core viewer-specific sections. Introduce URL sync. Wire the shared Accessibility section.

### Phase 4 — Polish & cross-app sync (WP-075, WP-077, WP-078)

Light mode, accent color, font scaling (shared Appearance section). Mobile bottom-sheet, viewer Advanced section, preset bundles, a11y audit. Cross-app preference sync via the `PrefsTransport` abstraction so shared-tier prefs can propagate to the future Legendary Arena game UI.

---

## 7. Bonus Recommendations

1. **Preference presets** — ship "Dense reviewer", "Presentation mode", "High-contrast" presets users can one-click apply.
2. **Per-device sync** — if the user is ever signed in to a BarefootBetters account, mirror prefs to an API endpoint so they follow the user across devices. Schema is already portable.
3. **Kbd-bindings editor** — reuse the shortcut-capture control from the Accessibility section to let users rebind `Ctrl+K` and `Ctrl+,`.
4. **Telemetry (opt-in)** — a single "Help improve Legendary Arena" toggle that, when on, sends anonymous preference histograms. Off by default; never on without explicit user action.
5. **Developer mode** — an Advanced toggle "I'm a developer" that reveals the diagnostics shortcut, raw-JSON card panel, and verbose `devLog`. Equivalent to today's `?debug` URL param but discoverable.
6. **Printable card grid** — Display-section toggle "Print-friendly mode" that switches to a light palette and hides non-essential chrome for screenshot / print workflows.
7. **Theme-aware accent** — when `themeMode === "system"`, listen to `window.matchMedia('(prefers-color-scheme: dark)')` and flip tokens live.
8. **Undo last change** — a small footer chip that appears for 10 seconds after any mutation and offers a one-click revert.

### WP-078 — Cross-app preference sync (shared tier) between viewer and game UI

- **Estimate:** 5
- **Dependencies:** WP-068, WP-075 (Appearance tier must exist before there's anything worth syncing)
- **Description:** Make the **shared-tier preferences** (Appearance, Accessibility, Advanced-base) propagate across the registry-viewer and the future Legendary Arena game UI. Implement **Option A (same-origin)** as the primary path and document **Options B and C** as escape hatches.

  **Option A — same-origin path routing (recommended):**
  - Deploy both apps under a single origin (e.g. `app.barefootbetters.com/cards` and `app.barefootbetters.com/play`).
  - `persistence.ts` uses `localStorage` directly; both apps read/write the same `legendary-arena.prefs.shared` key for shared-tier data, and separate `...viewer` / `...game` keys for private tiers.
  - A `storage` event listener in each app refreshes the in-memory store when the other app writes shared prefs in a different tab.

  **Option B — cross-subdomain via `postMessage` bridge:**
  - Invisible iframe hosted at a common origin (`prefs.barefootbetters.com`) acts as a broker.
  - Each app `postMessage`s shared-tier reads/writes to the iframe; the iframe owns the canonical `localStorage`.
  - Implementation stubbed behind a feature flag; not turned on until the game UI ships on a different subdomain.

  **Option C — account-backed server sync:**
  - Mirror shared-tier prefs to a `PATCH /api/preferences` endpoint when the user is signed in to a BarefootBetters account.
  - Last-write-wins with a `lastModifiedAt` timestamp per section.
  - Graceful offline: writes queue in IndexedDB and flush on reconnect.
  - Out of scope for this plan beyond adding the hook points; real implementation happens alongside account features.

  This WP delivers the **Option A** path end-to-end and creates the interfaces (`PrefsTransport`) the other two options slot into.

- **Acceptance criteria:**
  - Shared-tier keys (`appearance.*`, `accessibility.*`, `advancedBase.*`) persist under `legendary-arena.prefs.shared`; viewer-private keys under `legendary-arena.prefs.viewer`; game-private keys (when the game UI lands) under `legendary-arena.prefs.game`.
  - Changing `themeMode` from `dark` to `light` in one open tab of the viewer updates a second open tab (same origin) within 500 ms via the `storage` event.
  - `PrefsTransport` interface defined with `read()`, `write()`, and `subscribe()` methods; default implementation uses `localStorage`; alternate implementations for postMessage and HTTP exist as stub classes with unit-tested shapes.
  - Viewer continues to work if `PrefsTransport` is unavailable or times out (degrades to in-memory only).
  - Documentation: a short `packages/ui-preferences/CROSS-APP-SYNC.md` (or `apps/registry-viewer/src/prefs/CROSS-APP-SYNC.md` under Option A) explaining how to flip between Options A / B / C when the game UI ships.
  - No regression: running the viewer standalone with no game UI deployed produces the exact same UX as WP-077 delivered.
